the PXR signaling is not activated in rainbow trout by the tested substances.
the PXR in rainbow trout is not activated by any of the substances screened, but the CYP3a enzyme may be activated by some of these substances.
the PXR signaling in fish is more complex than previously assumed, and that it may be difficult to predict the effect of xenobiotics based on their ability to interact with PXR in other species.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the PXR in rainbow trout seems to be a weak receptor that is not easily activated by xenobiotics.
the PXR signaling is functional in rainbow trout and that it is affected by some prototypical agonists.
the effects of pharmaceuticals are complex and that they may not only be mediated through the PXR pathway, but also through other mechanisms.
The main takeaway from our work is that
PXR signaling in fish is more complex than in mammals and that the PXR pathway is not a good predictor for CYP3A induction in fish.
PXR activation in trout may not be the most relevant mechanism for the observed CYP3A induction in trout exposed to pharmaceuticals, and that CYP3A inducers may act via alternative pathways.
pharmaceuticals and other chemicals that activate PXR signaling in humans and rodents may not have similar effects on PXR signaling pathway of non-target animals, such as fish.
